<reason>A established the stronger distinction between liability for renting a vehicle and liability for an operator’s proven, preventable contribution to injury. Its suspension example directly answered B’s demands for advance-known duties without relying on precise GPS. B raised legitimate litigation and affordability concerns, but repeatedly inflated A’s limited standard into automatic corporate insurance and asserted inevitable jury overreach and service withdrawal. A also explained why regulatory fines do not replace compensation. B never convincingly established why rider misconduct erases responsibility when preventing that misconduct was the safeguard’s purpose.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A turned B’s account-ban proposal against its exclusive-control argument: companies control access, and clear suspension triggers remain knowable when damages are sought. B’s characterization of a knowingly ignored suspension as a “paperwork error” failed to answer A’s requirement that the breach actually contribute to the injury.</best_rebuttal>
